name: Git Suite
description: Grants agents controlled git capability through a per-command allowlist (each command tagged r/w/d with an independent enable toggle) plus a user-managed protected-branches guardrail, and holds the operator's git commit email used by the fallback author-vs-review heuristic.

allowedCommands.label: Allowed Commands
allowedCommands.description: Commands the agent is permitted to run. Toggle each row's Enabled checkbox to grant or revoke that specific command. The Category column labels the operation type: r = read-only (safe in all contexts), w = state-modifying but recoverable (commit, push, pull, etc.), d = destructive or history-rewriting (reset --hard, push --force, etc.). The Description column is a short reminder of what each command does — it's panel-only metadata and is not passed to the agent. Defaults grant all r commands plus the two branch commands 'git branch <name>' and 'git switch', and refuse everything else; enable individual w / d commands as needed for the task.

git blame.description: Show who last modified each line of a file and in which commit.

git branch.description: List local branches; mark the current branch with an asterisk.

git describe.description: Produce a human-readable name for the current commit using the nearest tag.

git diff.description: Show changes between commits, branches, working tree, etc.

git grep.description: Search tracked files for a pattern; faster than plain grep over the repo.

git log.description: Show commit history with messages, authors, and dates.

git ls-files.description: List files tracked by the index — useful for scoping searches.

git reflog.description: Show the local history of HEAD movements; lifeline for recovering lost commits.

git remote.description: List configured remotes and their URLs.

git rev-parse.description: Resolve a ref to its full SHA or show repo metadata paths.

git shortlog.description: Summarize git log output grouped by author.

git show.description: Display a commit, tag, or object along with its diff.

git stash list.description: List stashed changesets currently saved on the stash stack.

git status.description: Show working tree status — modified, staged, and untracked files.

git tag.description: List existing tags in the repository.

git add.description: Stage file contents for the next commit.

git apply.description: Apply a patch to files and/or the index without committing.

git branch <name>.description: Create a new local branch pointing at the current commit.

git cherry-pick.description: Apply the changes from existing commits onto the current branch.

git checkout.description: Switch branches (non-destructive form). Use 'git checkout -- <path>' for file-restore, which is a separate d-category entry.

git clone.description: Clone a repository into a new directory.

git commit.description: Record staged changes to the repository as a new commit.

git fetch.description: Download objects and refs from a remote without merging.

git init.description: Create an empty Git repository or reinitialize an existing one.

git merge.description: Join two or more development histories together into the current branch.

git mv.description: Move or rename a tracked file, directory, or symlink.

git pull.description: Fetch from a remote and integrate the changes into the current branch.

git push.description: Update a remote ref using the local ref's commits.

git rebase.description: Reapply commits on top of another base tip (non-interactive). Rewrites local unpublished commits; recoverable via reflog.

git remote add.description: Register a new remote repository under a short name.

git reset.description: Move HEAD and optionally update the index; safe modes preserve the working tree.

git restore --staged.description: Unstage paths from the index without touching the working tree.

git revert.description: Create a new commit that undoes the changes of an existing commit.

git rm --cached.description: Stop tracking a file — removes it from the index only and leaves it on disk. Nothing is lost.

git stash pop.description: Apply the latest stash and drop it from the stash stack.

git stash push.description: Save the current modified state onto a new stash entry.

git switch.description: Switch branches (modern replacement for the branch half of checkout).

git tag <name>.description: Create a new tag pointing at the current commit.

git branch -D.description: Force-delete a local branch even if it has unmerged commits.

git branch -d.description: Delete a local branch only when it is fully merged — git refuses while it still holds unmerged commits. Its own key: 'git branch -D' force-deletes and grants nothing here, and the read-only 'git branch' listing key grants neither.

git checkout -- <path>.description: Discard working-tree changes for the given path — uncommitted edits are lost.

git checkout -f.description: Switch branches while throwing away uncommitted working-tree changes — those edits are lost. Same flag as 'git checkout --force'; neither the plain 'git checkout' key nor the path-scoped 'git checkout -- <path>' key grants it.

git clean -f.description: Force-delete untracked files from the working tree.

git commit --amend.description: Replace the previous commit with a new one, rewriting it — the original is discarded, and amending an already-pushed commit needs a force-push to publish. Not granted by the plain 'git commit' key.

git filter-branch.description: Rewrite branch history wholesale by applying filters; deprecated and dangerous.

git push --delete.description: Delete a ref on the remote — removes the branch or tag for everyone.

git push --force.description: Force-push, overwriting remote history. Use with extreme care.

git rebase -i.description: Interactive rebase — reorder, squash, edit, or drop commits in local history.

git reset --hard.description: Reset HEAD and working tree — discards all uncommitted changes.

git rm.description: Remove tracked files from the index AND delete them from the working tree. Refuses on a file with uncommitted modifications; 'git rm -f' and 'git rm --cached' are separate entries and are not granted by this one.

git rm -f.description: Force-remove tracked files — deletes them even when they carry uncommitted modifications, so those edits are lost. Strictly more destructive than 'git rm'.

git stash clear.description: Delete every stash entry — the entire stash stack is wiped.

git stash drop.description: Delete a single stash entry from the stash stack.

git switch --discard-changes.description: Switch branches and throw local modifications away — uncommitted work is silently lost. One flag, three spellings: 'git switch -f', 'git switch --force', and 'git switch --discard-changes' all resolve to this entry and none of them is granted by the plain 'git switch' key.

git switch --merge.description: Switch branches and three-way merge local modifications into the destination — a real merge that can leave conflict markers in uncommitted work. Same flag as 'git switch -m'; not granted by the plain 'git switch' key, and reachable even when 'git merge' is disabled.

git switch -C <name>.description: Force-create a branch and switch to it — when a branch of that name already exists it is reset onto HEAD and the commits unique to it are dropped. Same flag as 'git switch --force-create'; the plain 'git switch' key covers only the safe lowercase '-c' create form and does not grant this one.

protectedBranches.label: Protected Branches
protectedBranches.description: Branches the agent must NOT modify regardless of which commands are enabled. Type a branch name plus an optional description, then click Add. An empty list means no branches are protected by this module.

commitMessageFormat.label: Commit Message Format
commitMessageFormat.description: Single-line template the agent fills in when you ask it to draft a commit message from the staged diff. Placeholders the agent substitutes: <TICKET> for the active ticket id if known, substituted bare, and <summary> for a concise one-line description. When no ticket is known, the <TICKET>: prefix (the ticket id, the colon, and the following space) is dropped cleanly, so the message is just the summary — never a leading colon or space. Keep this on one line; the Session Manifest renders each parameter as a single line, so a multi-line template reaches the agent malformed. Drafting is generation only — the agent hands the message back as text and never stages, commits, or pushes. Changing this changes how every future drafted message is worded.

gitEmail.label: Git Email
gitEmail.description: The operator's git commit email, used to refine the fallback author/review heuristic (compare against branch commit authors) when identity-based detection via integration.atlassian-suite's `bitbucketUsername` is unavailable. Optional; empty uses `git config user.email`. This is a non-secret identifier, not a credential.
